summary: CR-385 Phase 1 fresh QA (Role 4). BLOCKING ENV DRIFT: sandbox business date rolled from 2026-09-21 to Tuesday 2026-09-22 mid-run — the three pre-seeded pending direct bookings QA-R4-Cancel (225 · ...0011), QA-R4-Modify (226 · ...0012) and QA-R4-Legacy (227 · ...0013) are now in the LATE chip (LATE · SINCE 21 SEP), not Today. All Modify-preview / debounce / confirm mandates (P1-M2-03 → P1-M2-06) were NOT executable end-to-end because the debounced Modify+preview flow was designed for the Today chip and the test bookings sitting on the business date. P1-M2-02 cancel-inline (225) at 1920 was NOT executed for the same reason — could not open the Today chip, and the fd-chip-late testid was not found on the panel (chip DOM uses different testids than what the spec assumed). Nevertheless, M7 (Channel Manager › Front Desk Rules) SAVE cycle was exercised, captured, and verified in code+network: multipart/form-data POST with single 'data' part carrying the exact JSON body {"basic":{"allow_early_checkin":true,"extend_rate_mode":"calendar"}} was captured; toggle ON persisted across reload (early_checkin=true after reload). Sandbox is left CLEAN at end (early_checkin=false, extend_rate_mode=calendar, Saved, Save disabled — verified by reload). No rooms were touched. No No-Show confirm was clicked. No bookings were cancelled. The three seed bookings 225/226/227 were NOT cancelled — main agent must decide whether to (a) restore the business date to 2026-09-21, or (b) re-seed with fresh Today-side bookings, or (c) rewrite the Phase 1 acceptance to run against Late-chip rows. Additionally two new front-end concerns surfaced during M7 testing.

ui_bugs.issue: MAJOR (testability + a11y). Playwright page.click() and page.check() against the two extend-rate-mode radios do NOT trigger React onChange in this environment — the form stays clean, `dirty` stays false and frontdesk-rules-save-btn remains disabled after the click. Only a manual JS dispatch (input.click() via evaluate, or clicking the wrapping <label>) actually updates React state. Repro (viewport 1920x1080, Front Desk Rules tab, saved={cal=true,early=false}): `await page.click('[data-testid=radio-extend-rate-mode-held]')` → after 500 ms, radio-extend-rate-mode-held is_checked() === false, save-btn is_disabled() === true. Same for calendar recovery from held-selected state — needed a JS dispatch to flip. RCA hypothesis: the <label class="flex ... cursor-pointer"> wrapping the <input> intercepts the pointer event, Playwright targets the <input> element which is (a) rendered in-flow but visually indistinct or (b) receiving the pointer via bubble but React's synthetic 'change' event is being coalesced away. Users clicking the visible circle work fine; the risk is (i) automated tests can silently fail-open and (ii) screen-reader users driving via keyboard should be re-verified. Suggested fix: attach onClick handler on the label OR mark radios with `id` + label[for] wiring so both label and radio deliver clean click semantics; OR add data-testid to the enclosing label.

MINOR/NOTE. Spec assumed testids fd-chip-today, fd-chip-late, fd-chip-tomorrow, fd-chip-upcoming — page.click on those selectors timed out at 3s (locator not found). The chips ARE rendered (visible screenshot text 'Late 13 · Today 0 · Tomorrow 0 · Upcoming 4') so the DOM testids may differ from the spec (e.g. `fd-arrivals-chip-late` or without hyphens). Main agent should re-align the actual testid names with the spec used by tests. Not a functional bug per se, but blocks automated Late/Today chip switching until reconciled.

critical_code_review_comments: FrontDeskRulesTab.jsx (L60-66): the radio group ties `checked`+`onChange` on the <input> nested inside a <label>. Because there's no `id`/`htmlFor` pairing and the wrapping label is a display:flex block with a two-cell layout, some pointer paths (esp. programmatic clicks) don't reach the input's onChange in a deterministic way. Recommend `<input id="extend_rate_mode_calendar" …/> <label htmlFor="extend_rate_mode_calendar" …>` or an explicit onClick on the label that toggles the radio. This also improves keyboard/AT semantics.
